ideas.name: Top-of-screen banner in engine A Main Memory Display mode (DISPCNT mode 3) for the first N scanlines, fed by a DSi-only ARM9 NDMA channel from DScheevos RAM
ideas.mechanism: Engine A has two direct-colour display modes that skip the 2D/3D engines completely: mode 2 (VRAM display) and mode 3 (Main Memory Display). In mode 3, 15-bit pixels come from the Main Memory Display FIFO at 0x04000068, which a DMA in 'main memory display' mode feeds 4 words (8 pixels) at a time (gbatek 'DS Video Capture and Main Memory Display Mode', DISPCNT.16-17 table at gbatek.txt:7980-7988, DISP_MMEM_FIFO at :8187-8198). gbatek says the FIFO transfer 'starts at next frame' (:8197), so the DMA has to be armed in VBlank and the strip has to start at line 0. Per-frame sequence while a popup is up: (1) In VBlank (our existing ARM9 IPC-sync IRQ that ARM7 VBlank triggers), check the guards below. Arm ARM9 NDMA channel 2 or 3 (0x04004104+x*0x1C): SAD = banner buffer in 0x02D8xxxx main RAM, DAD = 0x04000068 fixed, startup mode 09h, WCNT=4, physical block 4 words, TCNT = N*128 words, 'repeat until TCNT' (NDMA regs at gbatek.txt:27942-27972). Set DISPCNT.16-17 = 3 with a read-modify-write of only those two bits. (2) Arm a second NDMA channel as a scanline counter: H-Blank startup (07h), fill-data source (no memory read), destination a private dummy word in module RAM, WCNT=1, TCNT about N-2, IRQ enable. Its NDMA IRQ (IE/IF bit 28-31, gbatek.txt:12844) fires near line N. The handler sets DISPCNT.16-17 back to the saved game value (1) with an RMW, again touching only those two bits. The N margin lines past the content are fed with banner-background pixels, so a late IRQ only makes the banner a few lines taller. (3) VBlank backstop: if DISPCNT.16-17 still reads 3 and we didn't expect it, put it back to 1. The banner is drawn in idle time (OS_Halt hook) into a double-buffered 256xN RGB555 buffer. It is either flushed from the data cache or written through the uncached 0x0Cxxxxxx mirror, because NDMA reads RAM and not the cache. On the CPU side, nothing touches VRAM, OAM, palettes, BG/OBJ registers, windows, blending or the 3D engine. Things that need not change: the game's own capture keeps working, because capture source A is taken from the engine output before the 'Select Video Input' stage (block diagram gbatek.txt:8205-8240). Master brightness still applies to mode 3 (:7986-7988), so the game's fades fade the banner too. The banner follows engine A to whichever panel POWCNT1 bit 15 picks (gbatek.txt:13664). Why not the game's VCOUNT IRQ: nds-bootstrap already does that for its colour-LUT feature (overrides LYC=0, cardengine.c:1671-1682) and needed a per-game block list for it (colorLutBlockVCount, cardengine.c:61).
ideas.resources_borrowed: (a) DISPCNT bits 16-17 only. DISPCNT is R/W, so before every show we read what the game set. We only act if the mode is 1 (graphics) and put back exactly the bits we changed. The lower halfword (layers, BG mode, windows) and bits 18-31 are never written with stale values. (b) DISPCAPCNT (R/W, gbatek.txt:8136) is only read. If the game has capture enabled with source B = FIFO (bit 25), the popup waits. (c) Legacy DMA 0-3 DMACNT (R/W) is only read: if a game channel is in mode 4 (main memory display, gbatek.txt:12725), the popup waits. FMV players and VRAM-display games fall into these waits. (d) ARM9 NDMA channels 2/3: DS-mode games are NTR binaries and cannot know NDMA exists. nds-bootstrap's CE9 already uses NDMA 0/1 for card reads in DS mode (cardDma.thumb.c:230,442), and bootloaderi turns on NDMA access for DS-mode games: REG_SCFG_EXT = 0x8300C000|BIT(16) (bootloaderi/source/arm9/main.arm9.c:395). (e) IE bits 28-31: these are not available today. That same SCFG_EXT9 value leaves bit 8 'Extended ARM9 Interrupts' clear, then locks SCFG (:402), so bootloaderi would have to add BIT(8) before the lock. (f) The IRQ vector: NitroSDK's dispatcher indexes its handler table by IRQ bit and was not written for bits 28-31. nds-bootstrap hooks table entries 2 and 16 (misc.c:116,120), not the vector. So the NDMA IRQ has to be caught by a wrapper installed at DTCM+0x3FFC that handles and acknowledges bits 28-31 and passes everything else on to the game's handler. The wrapper is re-checked every VBlank. Bit 28-31 is only enabled in IE while the wrapper is confirmed installed. (g) Bus: N*128 words per frame from main RAM, only while a popup is up. No VRAM bank, no OAM entry, no BG layer and no palette is used. That is the main difference from the bakkerrrs approach.
ideas.what_it_can_show: A full-width, fully opaque 256xN strip (for example N=32-48) on the engine-A panel, in 15-bit direct colour with no tile, palette or sprite limits. That covers RetroArch-style popups: unlock notice with a 32x32 or 64x64 full-colour badge (the stretch goal, decoded into module RAM in idle time), title and points; measured progress ('7/10'); challenge 'primed' notice; leaderboard started/failed/submitted plus the current value; the hardcore/softcore notice at game start. It cannot be partial-width or translucent, because mode 3 replaces whole scanlines. Leaderboard trackers and challenge indicators would be shown briefly when they change, not kept on screen, because a permanent strip would hide the top N lines of the game. Content is generated only from rc_client events, so it shows nothing RA wouldn't.
ideas.cost: ARM9 CPU: in VBlank, a few register reads and writes inside the existing IPC IRQ. One extra short IRQ per frame near line N (tens of instructions), only while a popup is up. Rendering happens in idle time (OS_Halt) once per popup change, then a cache flush of N*512 bytes (24 KB for N=48). Bus: the FIFO takes 4 words per 8 pixels and the dot clock is 6 cycles per pixel (gbatek.txt:7828-7831), so 128 words per line, 6144 words (24 KB) per frame for N=48. All of it falls inside the first N lines and there is no traffic outside popups. ARM7: nothing. Memory: 2 x 24 KB banner buffers plus a font and badge cache in the module heap. A bottom strip would need the whole frame fed (96 KB/frame, roughly 9% of main-RAM bus time) because of the 'starts at next frame' rule, which is why the strip is at the top.
ideas.known_risks: Ranked. (1) It is not documented whether DISPCNT.16-17 is latched per scanline. gbatek says nothing about changing the display mode mid-frame. melonDS reads DispCnt on every line (GPU_Soft.cpp:211), but that is emulator behaviour, not proof. If real hardware latches it per frame, the idea fails (full screen only). This is the first test to run: a libnds homebrew on a real DSi that switches mode 3 to mode 1 at a VCOUNT IRQ. (2) NDMA startup mode 09h is marked 'Work RAM (what?) (=probably Main memory display, as on NDS)' (gbatek.txt:27968). melonDS maps it to the display FIFO (DSi.cpp:52-60), so the bench works, but hardware has to confirm it. Second cheap homebrew test. (3) The switch back to mode 1 needs an IRQ that nds-bootstrap doesn't support today: bootloaderi needs SCFG_EXT9 bit 8, plus a wrapper at the DTCM+0x3FFC vector. A game that rewrites the vector after boot, or runs with IRQs off for a long stretch, makes the switch late. Each late line shows banner margin first, then FIFO underrun pixels for the rest of that one frame. The VBlank backstop limits this to one frame. It is a visible glitch, though it changes no game state. (4) DISPCNT read-modify-write race: if the game reads DISPCNT during the strip (sees mode 3), our IRQ fires, and then the game writes its copy back, mode 3 stays on below the strip for that frame. Bench step: add a DISPCNT write log (PC, VCOUNT) to the melonDS fork and count mid-frame DISPCNT writes for each target game. A game that writes it often in lines 0..N goes on a no-banner list. (5) IE overwrite: a game that writes the whole IE register (OS_SetIrqMask style) clears bit 28-31 and the IRQ is lost. Mitigation is to re-assert it every VBlank, as CE9 already does for IPC_SYNC/VCOUNT (cardengine.c:1775-1790). A loss in the middle of a frame still goes through (3). (6) Covering the top N lines of engine A can hide HUD elements (score, timer), and on games that put engine A on the touch panel, it can hide touch targets for the length of the popup. Touch input itself is not affected. Keep popups short (about 3 s), make the position and size configurable, and allow leaderboard popups to be turned off (RA allows that). (7) Not portable to B4DS on a DS: no NDMA, no 0x02D80000 RAM, so it would have to borrow a game-owned legacy DMA channel in mode 4. Reading DMACNT shows whether a channel is idle, but the game could start it at any moment. Treat it as DSi-only. (8) An emulator result does not settle (1) and (2). Running this in melonDS validates our code path, not the hardware behaviour.

ideas.name: Show the hardcore/softcore notice (and set summary) on nds-bootstrap's pre-boot screen, before the game owns the hardware
ideas.mechanism: bootloaderi's ARM9 already runs a small state machine that draws full-screen text and images before handing over to the game. The ESRB screen calls arm9_esrbScreen, fades in, and waits waitFrames(60*3) (a minimum of 3 seconds). The 'Please wait' screen calls arm9_pleaseWaitText and fadeIn (retail/bootloaderi/source/arm9/main.arm9.c:307-345). Add one more state, for example ARM9_DISPRA, that the ARM7 side sets when a session.bin was accepted. It draws 'RetroAchievements - HARDCORE' (or Softcore), the game title, 'x/y achievements, z points', and optionally the game icon or badge already in the session file. Show it for about 2 s with the same fade helpers, then continue the normal boot. The DScheevos launcher, which does login and session start before nds-bootstrap, can show the same line on its own screen. The bootloader is the last screen before the game, though, so it is the one that matches 'when the player starts a game'.
ideas.resources_borrowed: None of the game's. At this point the game isn't running: the bootloader owns both engines, VRAM, palettes and the display, as it already does for the ESRB notice. Everything is reset before the game's entry point, as it is today.
ideas.what_it_can_show: The required hardcore-state notice at game start, word for word what the compliance text calls the 'normal' way: 'a brief informational message saying what mode they're in'. It can also show set totals, the player's progress so far, and whether DScheevos is online. It cannot show anything during play, so it only covers this one acceptance item. Unlocks, progress, challenge and leaderboard notices need idea 1, or the existing LED plus in-game menu.
ideas.cost: About 2 s more on the boot path, only when a DScheevos session is active. Nothing per frame. Code goes into bootloaderi, which already has a font and image renderer for the ESRB and error screens.
ideas.known_risks: Some players may find the extra boot delay annoying: make the length configurable, never zero in hardcore. The text needs the mode from session.bin, which the bootloader already passes to the module, so this is only plumbing. The RA reviewer may also want the mode visible later in the session; the in-game menu's Achievements page already shows it (architecture.md 'What the player sees').
ideas.evidence: nds-bootstrap retail/bootloaderi/source/arm9/main.arm9.c:59-65 (ESRB state), :124 (fadeIn), :307-326 (ESRB screen with waitFrames(60*3)), :330-345 (Please-wait and error screens). dscheevos docs/architecture.md 'Session start' steps 3-4 (bootloader receives the session) and 'What the player sees'.

ideas.name: Translucent overlay with capture blending and VRAM display (DISPCAPCNT A+B blend into an LCDC bank, shown with display mode 2). Evaluated and rejected, together with windows/blending, master brightness, extended palettes, VRAM H/I and the 3D quad
ideas.mechanism: How it would work: each frame, set DISPCAPCNT (0x04000064) to capture source = A+B blended (bits 29-30 = 2), source A = graphics screen (bit 24 = 0), source B = Main Memory FIFO (bit 25 = 1) fed by NDMA from the banner buffer, EVA/EVB set for about 60/40 alpha, size 256x192, write block = a VRAM bank A-D mapped to LCDC (MST=0). Engine A is then switched to display mode 2 (DISPCNT.16-17 = 2, block in bits 18-19), so the player sees the previous frame's capture: the game blended with the overlay, the RetroArch look. gbatek describes this capture-and-display-next-frame loop (gbatek.txt:8136-8186, notes at :8172-8186).
ideas.resources_borrowed: A whole 128 KB bank (A, B, C or D) has to sit in LCDC mode for as long as the overlay is up, and capture is engine A's only capture unit. VRAMCNT_A..I are write-only (gbatek.txt:7081, each marked (W)). No hardware read can prove the game isn't using a bank, so the only options are shadowing the game's writes or reading NitroSDK's own bank bookkeeping. That is the 'is this free?' guessing that failed on Ketsui in the bakkerrrs project. 3D games often use capture themselves (dual-screen 3D, motion blur), which conflicts outright.
ideas.what_it_can_show: Any translucent full-colour overlay anywhere on engine A's screen. Visually the best option, but not safely achievable.
ideas.cost: With the bank problem set aside: 1 frame of extra display latency on engine A for the whole popup, which is input lag the owner would rightly count as a gameplay issue. Plus 96 KB/frame of FIFO feed for a full-screen blend, and 6-cycle VRAM write contention from capture (gbatek 'VRAM Waitstates', just after :7843).
ideas.known_risks: Not viable on this evidence: it needs an unprovable free 128 KB bank and adds a frame of latency. The other sub-angles in the brief fail for the same kind of reason. WINDOWS + BLENDING to darken a strip: WIN0H/WIN0V and BLDY are write-only (gbatek.txt:615,625,1258), so we can neither read back nor restore the game's values. Per-line changes would wipe out the game's own window and fade effects. BLDCNT and WININ are R/W, but darkening needs BLDY. And dimming alone draws no text. MASTER BRIGHTNESS (0x0400006C/0x0400106C, gbatek.txt:7836-7843): one factor for a whole engine, no spatial control. Rewriting it per line from an H-Blank NDMA would give a dimmed band but could not draw anything, and it fights game fades. At most it could serve as a backdrop for idea 1, which is opaque and doesn't need one. EXTENDED PALETTES and VRAM H/I (H 32 KB to engine-B BG or BG ext-palette, I 16 KB to engine-B BG/OBJ/OBJ ext-palette): these only show through engine B's own layers and sprites, which the game owns. Their VRAMCNT is also write-only, so it is the same inference problem bakkerrrs hit. There is no extra DSi-only VRAM: in DS mode the DSi has exactly banks A-I, and SCFG_EXT9 bit 13 'Extended VRAM Access' only changes access timing (the in-game menu offers it as 'boost VRAM', inGameMenu.c:557,674). 3D ENGINE (one textured quad on top, or the rear plane): the geometry FIFO, matrix stacks, polygon/vertex RAM, texture slots and the rear-plane image (texture slots 2/3) all belong to games that use 3D. Adding a polygon to the game's display list risks its state and its polygon budget. 2D-only games would need 3D enabled on BG0, taking a game layer. Rejected.
